title: Knowledge and its opposite (13.7–13.18)
hook: the Gita's list of what knowledge is starts with something you can't look up

segments.voice: Yesterday: the body is the field, and there's a knower at its edge. Your line was the field. Did you catch something growing there? Today, what the knower actually knows. Day two hundred five.

Picture the smartest person you know. Maybe they have three degrees. Maybe they win every argument at dinner. Now picture the wisest person you know. Often it isn't the same person. The wise one might have no degree at all. They just listen longer, and they don't need to be right. The Gita has noticed this too. In chapter thirteen Krishna gives a list with the heading knowledge. You'd expect facts, or philosophy, or a curriculum. Instead the list opens with something no exam can test.
screen: `THE SMARTEST PERSON YOU KNOW.` → `THE WISEST PERSON YOU KNOW.` → `NOT ALWAYS THE SAME.`

segments.voice: Verse seven. The first word on the list is amanitva: humility, not thinking much of yourself. Then adambhitva, no pretending. Then ahimsa, doing no harm, a word you met in camp one. Then patience, straightforwardness, serving your teacher, cleanliness, steadiness, self-control. The list keeps going. Not being dragged by the senses. Not being ruled by the sense of I. Seeing clearly that birth, age, sickness and death bring pain. Not clinging too tightly to home and family. Staying even when things go well and when they don't. Steady devotion. A taste for quiet places, and less need for the crowd. Twenty or so qualities, and Krishna ends with a surprise. This, he says, is called knowledge. And whatever is the opposite of this is ajnana, ignorance. So in the Gita, knowledge isn't only what's in your head. It's what shows in how you live. A brilliant, arrogant person, by this definition, is missing the first item. Then from verse twelve the chapter turns to what is to be known, Brahman, and the description goes strange on purpose. It has hands and feet everywhere, eyes and faces everywhere. It shines through every sense, yet has no senses. It's far away, and it's near. It's inside beings and outside them. It seems divided among beings, yet it's undivided. Verse seventeen calls it the light of lights, beyond darkness. The words are stretching to point at something words can't hold. And the door to it, the list says, starts with humility. That's the word today: knowledge and its opposite.
screen: `FIRST ON THE LIST: HUMILITY.` · `KNOWLEDGE IS HOW YOU LIVE.` · `THE OPPOSITE IS IGNORANCE.` · `FAR AND NEAR, THE LIGHT OF LIGHTS.` · then, large: `KNOWLEDGE AND ITS OPPOSITE.`

segments.voice: Sit, and think of a recent moment you needed to be right. A text thread, a meeting, a family dinner. Don't judge it. Just see it. Now picture that same moment, and let the need drop by one notch. Maybe you ask a question instead of making a point. Maybe you simply listen. Breathe into that softer version. Notice how it feels in the chest. That softness is the first item on the Gita's list. The bell holds the time.
Knowledge and its opposite. Gita thirteen, seven to eighteen: knowledge is a way of living that begins with humility, and its opposite is ignorance.
Your line: humility first. Today, in one conversation, let someone else be right, or ask one real question before you answer. Day two hundred five.

screen: `DAY 205 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: SEEING THE SAME IN ALL.`

howItsDone: Hindu teachers often quote Gita 13.7–13.11 as a checklist of character for students, starting with amanitva, humility; many traditions treat serving and honoring the teacher as part of this knowledge.

match.prompt: what's on the list of knowledge — tap the pairs.

myth: the Gita's list of 'knowledge' is mostly facts and doctrines
it's mostly qualities of character: humility, patience, steadiness, no harm.
the first word on the list is humility
amanitva: not thinking much of yourself.
verse 17 calls what is to be known the light of lights
the light of lights, beyond darkness.

fork.setup: Krishna has listed twenty qualities and called them knowledge. what does he call their opposite?
fork.reveal: ajnana, ignorance. in this chapter, the opposite of knowledge is a way of living, not a wrong answer.

original.note: Sanskrit: amanitva, humility, literally not-being-proud; the first item in Gita 13's list of knowledge.

trapdoor: what you thought: knowledge means knowing a lot.
what it means: in Gita 13, knowledge is a list of qualities, humility first, and ignorance is their opposite.
what a scholar hears: 13.7–13.11 lists roughly twenty qualities beginning 'amanitvam adambhitvam ahimsa'; 13.11 calls them jnana and the rest ajnana.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 13.7–13.11 (the list of knowledge; the rest is ignorance)
Bhagavad Gita 13.12–13.17 (what is to be known; light of lights)

notes: All verses paraphrased. Verse numbers follow the edition without the extra opening verse; check against the path's edition.
'Twenty or so qualities': counts differ by commentator (commonly twenty).
The 'not clinging too tightly to home and family' line paraphrases 13.9; check tone.
